**Description**
 Applied Scientists on the AWS Vulnerability Management (AVM) Builder Enablement team use program analysis, machine learning and generative AI for managing vulnerabilities and securing the software supply chain across AWS. Our scope covers the third\-party open\-source packages, language ecosystems, operating systems and kernels that AWS services are built on. Our goal is to take builders out of the remediation loop. When a vulnerability is disclosed or a package is compromised, our systems work out whether it actually affects AWS, generate the fix, check that it's safe and ship it at AWS scale, with one click or no clicks at all.
   

  

 New vulnerabilities are disclosed every day in the software AWS depends on, and finding and fixing them by hand doesn't scale. We build systems that detect vulnerabilities and work out whether the vulnerable code can actually be reached and exploited in a given service. They rank issues by real risk rather than raw severity scores, then fix them automatically. That can mean upgrading dependencies across ecosystems like Java, Python, JavaScript, Go and Rust, fixing breaking API changes, backporting patches, or patching operating systems and kernels across the fleet. Just as important, we check that each fix is correct and safe, so it can merge with little or no human review.
   

  

 Beyond known vulnerabilities, we protect the integrity of the software supply chain itself. Modern software is assembled more than it is written, and every dependency is a potential way in for attackers. Securing it means knowing what's in our software, where it came from and whether it can be trusted. Our work here includes building and analyzing software bills of materials (SBOMs), verifying package provenance and build integrity, and detecting malicious or compromised packages before they reach production.
   

  

 Our methods range from static and dynamic program analysis to LLM\-based agents for code repair and upgrades. This is a chance to shape a fast\-growing area that directly affects the security of AWS and its customers. You'll apply your technical depth in a fast\-moving environment, and your work will reach thousands of AWS builders and services.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

* Design and build scientific approaches to vulnerability management. This includes vulnerability detection, reachability and exploitability analysis, dependency resolution, and prioritizing risk across third\-party packages, operating systems and kernels.
* Build program analysis techniques (static analysis, dataflow and call\-graph analysis, binary and source analysis) that tell us precisely whether a vulnerability affects a given service or host.
* Apply generative AI and agentic coding methods to fix vulnerabilities automatically. Examples include upgrading dependencies, fixing breaking API changes, backporting patches and migrating code across language versions.
* Develop ways to check that automated fixes are correct and safe, such as test generation, behavior\-equivalence checking, build and runtime checks, and confidence scoring, so changes can merge with little or no human review.
* Own the design, experiments and delivery of well\-defined science problems from start to finish. Turn ambiguous problems into measurable experiments and deliver solutions with measurable impact, such as faster time to fix, higher fix success rates and fewer false positives.
* Work with engineers to turn research prototypes into production systems that run reliably across AWS's codebases and fleet.
* Work with security, OS and kernel, and builder\-tools partner teams to understand their remediation challenges and data. Find opportunities where science can make a difference.
* Stay current with research in software security, program analysis, and ML for code. Contribute to internal and external publications where appropriate.
* Share your knowledge through design reviews, documentation and mentoring of junior scientists and engineers.


**About The Team**
 The AWS Vulnerability Management (AVM) Builder Enablement team protects AWS from security risks in the software it depends on. Our mission is to take builders out of the remediation loop. We find the issues that matter, fix them automatically and ship the fixes safely at AWS scale. Scientists and engineers on the team work side by side, turning research in program analysis and generative AI into production systems that reach thousands of AWS builders.

**Description**
 Applied Scientists on the AWS Vulnerability Management (AVM) Builder Enablement team use program analysis, machine learning and generative AI for managing vulnerabilities and securing the software supply chain across AWS. Our scope covers the third\-party open\-source packages, language ecosystems, operating systems and kernels that AWS services are built on. Our goal is to take builders out of the remediation loop. When a vulnerability is disclosed or a package is compromised, our systems work out whether it actually affects AWS, generate the fix, check that it's safe and ship it at AWS scale, with one click or no clicks at all.
   

  

 New vulnerabilities are disclosed every day in the software AWS depends on, and finding and fixing them by hand doesn't scale. We build systems that detect vulnerabilities and work out whether the vulnerable code can actually be reached and exploited in a given service. They rank issues by real risk rather than raw severity scores, then fix them automatically. That can mean upgrading dependencies across ecosystems like Java, Python, JavaScript, Go and Rust, fixing breaking API changes, backporting patches, or patching operating systems and kernels across the fleet. Just as important, we check that each fix is correct and safe, so it can merge with little or no human review.
   

  

 Beyond known vulnerabilities, we protect the integrity of the software supply chain itself. Modern software is assembled more than it is written, and every dependency is a potential way in for attackers. Securing it means knowing what's in our software, where it came from and whether it can be trusted. Our work here includes building and analyzing software bills of materials (SBOMs), verifying package provenance and build integrity, and detecting malicious or compromised packages before they reach production.
   

  

 Our methods range from static and dynamic program analysis to LLM\-based agents for code repair and upgrades. This is a chance to shape a fast\-growing area that directly affects the security of AWS and its customers. You'll apply your technical depth in a fast\-moving environment, and your work will reach thousands of AWS builders and services.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

* Design and build scientific approaches to vulnerability management. This includes vulnerability detection, reachability and exploitability analysis, dependency resolution, and prioritizing risk across third\-party packages, operating systems and kernels.
* Build program analysis techniques (static analysis, dataflow and call\-graph analysis, binary and source analysis) that tell us precisely whether a vulnerability affects a given service or host.
* Apply generative AI and agentic coding methods to fix vulnerabilities automatically. Examples include upgrading dependencies, fixing breaking API changes, backporting patches and migrating code across language versions.
* Develop ways to check that automated fixes are correct and safe, such as test generation, behavior\-equivalence checking, build and runtime checks, and confidence scoring, so changes can merge with little or no human review.
* Own the design, experiments and delivery of well\-defined science problems from start to finish. Turn ambiguous problems into measurable experiments and deliver solutions with measurable impact, such as faster time to fix, higher fix success rates and fewer false positives.
* Work with engineers to turn research prototypes into production systems that run reliably across AWS's codebases and fleet.
* Work with security, OS and kernel, and builder\-tools partner teams to understand their remediation challenges and data. Find opportunities where science can make a difference.
* Stay current with research in software security, program analysis, and ML for code. Contribute to internal and external publications where appropriate.
* Share your knowledge through design reviews, documentation and mentoring of junior scientists and engineers.

 The AWS Vulnerability Management (AVM) Builder Enablement team protects AWS from security risks in the software it depends on. Our mission is to take builders out of the remediation loop. We find the issues that matter, fix them automatically and ship the fixes safely at AWS scale. Scientists and engineers on the team work side by side, turning research in program analysis and generative AI into production systems that reach thousands of AWS builders.

**About The Role**
 TRG builds production software where AI agents generate much of the code and engineers own the outcome. We're hiring an experienced software engineer who writes clear specifications, directs AI agents to build against them, and is accountable for whether the result is correct, secure, and maintainable.
   

  

 AI changes where your time goes, not what you're responsible for. You'll spend more time on requirements, decomposition, review, and validation, and less on writing code by hand. You'll still need the engineering depth to read, debug, and fix code you didn't write.
   

  

 You'll work alongside TRG's AI engineering team and business stakeholders, and you'll be expected to own delivery from day one.
   

  

****What This Role Is, and Is Not****
**This Role Is**
* A hands\-on software engineering role with real production accountability.
* Built around spec\-driven development: you define what "done" means, then drive AI agents to get there.
* Responsible for correctness, security, performance, and maintainability, regardless of who or what wrote the code.


**This Role Is Not**
* A prompt\-only or non\-technical position.
* A research, data science, or model\-training role.
* An entry\-level or training position.


****What You'll Do****
**Specify and decompose**
* Turn business requests into structured specs: scope, out\-of\-scope, acceptance criteria, and validation rules.
* Break complex work into tasks agents can execute reliably, with traceability back to the requirement.


**Orchestrate agents**
* Direct AI agents to build, configure, integrate, test, and troubleshoot software systems.
* Give agents the documentation, system context, tools, permissions, and constraints they need, and no more access than required.
* Coordinate work across agents, manage dependencies, and resolve conflicting or incomplete results.
* Run multiple agent workstreams in parallel on isolated branches and integrate their results safely.
* Recognize when an agent is stuck, making unsupported assumptions, or solving the wrong problem, and redirect it.


**Review and validate**
* Review AI\-generated and human\-written code for architecture, security, performance, and maintainability.
* Catch hallucinations, logic gaps, and unsafe patterns before they reach production.
* Build agents and automated harnesses that test, verify, and iterate on their own code: writing and running tests, reading failures, and fixing issues before work reaches human review.
* Ensure unit, integration, and regression test coverage, using AI to accelerate test generation while verifying the tests themselves.
* Validate outcomes through testing, logs, automated checks, and comparison against business requirements.


**Ship and operate**
* Ship every change through merge requests with CI gates.
* Deploy through CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure as code, following established security, approval, and rollback procedures.
* Investigate production issues and determine whether the cause is instructions, data, tooling, or the underlying system.
* Monitor post\-deployment behavior and close the loop on defects.


**Make it repeatable**
* Build and maintain reusable specs, prompts, guardrails, and review checklists so successful workflows produce consistent results across the team.
* Contribute to TRG's standards for AI\-assisted development.


**Required Qualifications**
* 3\+ years of professional software engineering experience building and owning production systems (backend services, APIs, integrations, or applications), including releases and incident support.
* Daily, hands\-on use of agentic development tools such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, or Codex on real work. Be prepared to walk us through a specific example.
* Demonstrated ability to read, reason about, and debug code you didn't write.
* Experience directing AI agents to write and run tests against acceptance criteria, read failures, and iterate before work reaches human review.
* Working knowledge of Git, automated testing, and CI/CD pipelines.
* Hands\-on experience writing and maintaining YAML for CI/CD pipelines and deployment configuration (GitLab CI or similar), along with infrastructure as code (Bicep or Terraform).
* Experience building and deploying on a major cloud platform.
* Professional proficiency in at least one of C\#, TypeScript, or Python.
* Understanding of secure coding practices and handling sensitive data, including risks specific to AI agents such as prompt injection, secret leakage, and over\-broad permissions.
* Clear written communication: specs and documentation that people and agents can act on.
* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.


**Preferred Qualifications**
* Experience with Microsoft Azure.
* Working knowledge of C\#/.NET, TypeScript (Node, React or Angular), Python, and SQL (SQL Server preferred).
* Experience building agent harnesses, self\-verification loops, or evaluations that check agent output against defined acceptance criteria.
* Spec\-driven development experience (e.g., Kiro spec workflows, GitHub Spec Kit, or similar).
* Multi\-agent orchestration, MCP servers, or building AI\-integrated workflows.
* Experience in a regulated industry: title, mortgage, insurance, or financial services.
* Experience working in Agile teams.


****What Success Looks Like****
 You deliver working outcomes with evidence that they meet the requirements. For any piece of work, you can explain what was requested, how you directed the agents, how you verified the result, and what risk remains. You verify results rather than accept a confident answer, and you know when to proceed, ask, or stop. You independently own projects end to end and escalate only the decisions that need additional business or architectural judgment.

**About Us**
 Mintive helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. That has to start from trust. Our first product is an MCP gateway that gives those agents governed access to company data and tools.
   

  

 Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. Our gateway product scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long\-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on.
   

  

 We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how.
   

  

 We are AI\-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team and handle sales, marketing, deal ops, and engineering on the same gateway we sell to customers, and we are building an entire company operating system around them.
   

  

 Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 50\+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. Our founders are machine learning experts from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU, with applied research at Google Brain and Waymo, and one co\-founded Coursera.
   

  

****The Job****
 You will own features end to end, from conception to production, across our gateway infrastructure, enterprise deployments, and agentic systems. The work leans backend and infra, but nothing is off limits: when the product needs a better UI you build it, and when a connector breaks during a security review you fix it.
   

  

 Claude and Codex are your primary working environment, and you use a fleet of agents to move faster than a team this size has any right to. Agents write much of the code and review PRs, so your real job is the judgment they cannot make: shaping the problem, making architecture, product, and UX calls, hardening enterprise paths, designing connectors, protecting security\-sensitive surfaces, and catching generated code that is quietly wrong. Roles are blurred and we ship within hours, and you will learn directly from the founders and from customers.
   

  

 We hire across levels, from strong early\-career builders to seasoned engineers, and we set level and pay to match. What matters most is judgment, range, and how fast you ship.

* You are a builder with a track record of shipping to real users, whether that is a product, an internal tool, an open\-source project, or a serious side project. You ship, then iterate, without waiting for specs or approvals.
* You have strong fundamentals and learn fast. How quickly you pick things up matters as much as years of experience.

Unlike academia, our scientists have long-term funding and industry-like resources. Unlike industry, they're free to pursue high-risk, long-term research without commercial pressures. Arc's Technology Centers and Core Investigator labs work side by side, integrating experimental and computational biology under one roof to tackle problems neither could solve alone.
Our two Institute Initiatives reflect this model in action:
Virtual Cell Initiative : Building a full-stack virtual cell model to identify disease mechanisms and nominate drug targets,  accelerating the path from biological insight to clinical trials.
Alzheimer's Disease Initiative : Mapping the genes, pathways, and environmental factors behind Alzheimer's disease to develop drug candidates that address root causes.
More than 300 Arconauts work together at our Palo Alto headquarters, backed by substantial long-term philanthropic funding.
About the position
You'll join Arc's Infrastructure Engineering team and own support and operations for our laboratory information management system (LIMS). Arc's scientists record their samples and experiments there, including the variables they change from one experiment to the next. That record is business intelligence for the lab: it's how scientists learn which conditions improve an assay, and it also feeds the pipelines that process lab data automatically. You'll run the request queue, make schema changes, train users and maintain the checks on data as it's entered, and you'll turn the requests that keep coming back into automation. You don't need LIMS experience: strong Python and SQL and an interest in lab data matter more, and we'll teach you the platform. You'll start under our lab platform Tech Lead, who will review your work and mentor you.
Why this position could be the best job you’ve ever had
Your work reaches the lab within a week, and it shows up in results: the experiment records you keep accurate are how labs find what makes their assays perform better.
You'll learn how a research institute turns lab work into data, with a Tech Lead whose goal is to hand you more of the system as you grow.
About you
You finish what you own, and you fix what's broken without being asked.
You're curious about the biology and the mission. You want to know what a guide or a 10x Flex run is.
You go to the scientists. You sit down with them, learn how they run and record their experiments, and understand what they need before you propose a fix.
You're careful and thoughtful. You want more scope and you'll take it on before you have every skill it needs, and you double-check changes other teams depend on.
You see which requests need a general solution, and you balance that work with the rest of the queue.

Run the request queue for Arc's lab data systems, from questions and fixes to schema changes, which you'll ship through our change workflow so other teams' pipelines don't break.
Support the templates scientists record experiments with, and the command-line tools that pull their data for analysis.
Run training sessions for scientists, and write the docs they come back to.
Build and maintain the checks that catch errors in data as scientists enter it, so bad records don't reach analysis or pipelines.
Help carry out the refactor of the team and permission structure in our LIMS, which decides who can see and edit what.
Turn the requests that keep coming back into automation, and choose the approach that fits the problem: a script, a scheduled job, a template change or an AI agent. Write the runbook, add the checks and retire the manual step; changes go through the team's code review.

 Seed\-stage AI company backed by a top\-tier venture firm
 



  





**About the company** 




 Our client is building an agentic service desk for managed service providers the firms that run IT for small and midsized businesses worldwide, a category representing roughly half a trillion dollars in annual spend. Their AI agents sit alongside human technicians: reading tickets, investigating root causes across the tools MSPs already run on, and executing approved fixes.
 



  





 The engineering problem is genuinely hard. These agents have to reason through problems no one wrote a runbook for, respect customer policy, carry state across workflows that run for hours or days, and behave predictably inside live production environments. The company closed a seed round from a tier\-one venture firm and is now hiring the engineers who will define how the product actually works.
 



  





**The opportunity** 




 The Founding AI Engineer will own the agent layer end to end — from first prototype through hardened production deployment. The work rotates by nature: one week may go toward teaching an agent to diagnose an unfamiliar failure mode, the next toward building evaluation harnesses that surface where it breaks down, the next toward the tooling and infrastructure that let it act safely inside a customer's stack.
 



  





 This is a builder's seat, not an architect's. The person in this role will talk to customers directly, help set the roadmap, ship the code, and operate what they ship. They will also help settle the open questions in this category which decisions belong to agents, where humans keep the final call, how agent reasoning gets explained to a technician, and what a genuinely good technician experience looks like. Those standards are unwritten today. This role helps write them.
 



  





**What the role involves** 



* Building and refining AI agents that investigate IT issues, hold context over long sessions, call tools across customer systems, operate within policy, escalate for approval, and recover cleanly when something goes wrong.
* Standing up evaluation systems that quantify agent quality, surface failure modes, and convert production traces and customer feedback into concrete improvements.
* Running fast experiments across models, prompting strategies, retrieval, tool design, and agent architectures — then promoting what works into dependable production systems.
* Engineering the integrations and backend infrastructure that let agents run securely, reliably, and observably through long\-lived customer workflows.
* Working directly with customers to understand their day\-to\-day, shipping product improvements end to end, and helping establish engineering practices as the team grows.



  





**Who this is a fit for** 



* Engineers who have shipped production software built on modern AI models: agents or other tool\-using systems especially.
* People who move quickly with new models and techniques and can carry a promising prototype through to something reliable.
* Engineers comfortable evaluating nondeterministic systems, debugging failures without clean stack traces, and trading speed against quality, safety, and customer trust deliberately rather than by accident.
* Strong ownership, deep personal use of AI tooling, real product instincts, and comfort sitting in front of a customer and turning a vague problem into working software.

**Description**
 At Amazon Web Services (AWS), Security is our highest priority. AWS Vulnerability Management (AVM) is accountable for the end to end vulnerability lifecycle across all of AWS: finding, contextualizing, and assessing vulnerabilities, and driving remediation at machine speed, without manual work from builders and at the lowest cost to AWS.
   

  

 The Remediation Engineering Team (PitCrew) builds and operates the capabilities that close the gap between a finding being known and it being gone. Our mandate is to automate mitigation, remediation, and assessment. We develop capabilities for mitigation and remediation outside of patching: recognizing potentially vulnerable and unused software components and retiring them on behalf of service teams, delivering remediations to builders as changes they can review and approve, and acting on hosts and their payloads within minutes when a patch is unavailable or too slow. We also build the tooling AVM security engineers use to codify, classify, and track the blockers that keep service teams from remediating on time, and the automation behind assessment and attestation: contextualizing findings with asset\-level signals such as network reachability and compensating controls so that severity reflects true risk and every critical finding is a true critical, attesting to accepted residual risk, and generating evidence of those decisions continuously for auditors and customers.
   

  

 As a Software Development Engineer II on PitCrew, you will design, build, and operate services that act on hosts and containers across AWS at fleet scale. You will own features end to end: working with security engineers to understand a problem, writing the design, implementing it, deploying it, and operating what you ship. The work sits at the intersection of distributed systems, host and container internals, and security, and much of it is about making changes to production systems safely and reversibly at scale.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

* Design, implement, and operate services and automation that mitigate, remediate, and assess vulnerabilities across AWS fleets, reducing the attack surface and mean time to remediate without a human in the loop.
* Build the contextualization that turns raw findings into accurate, prioritized risk for builders, so service teams act on true criticals first.
* Own the full lifecycle of your software: requirements, design reviews, implementation, testing, deployment, metrics, alarms, and on\-call.
* Build tooling that security engineers use daily, and work closely with them to turn investigation, remediation, assessment, and attestation workflows into software.
* Make changes to production hosts and containers safe by default: reversible, observable, attested, and gated appropriately.
* Raise the bar on operational excellence through metrics, dashboards, and continuous improvement of the systems you own.
* Mentor other engineers and contribute to the team's technical direction through design reviews and documentation.


 A day in the life
   

  

 You will spend most of your time designing and writing software, reviewing designs and code from teammates, and working with AVM security engineers and the partner teams that consume what we build. You will participate in the team's on\-call rotation for the services we operate.

**About Retool**
 Nearly every company in the world runs on custom software for critical operations like tracking performance metrics, handling support workflows, building admin dashboards, and countless processes you might never have thought of. But most companies don't have the resources to properly invest in these tools, leading to a lot of old, clunky internal software, or worse, teams still stuck in manual and spreadsheet workflows.
   

  

 AI has changed who gets to build software. The definition of "developer" now includes analysts, operators, and domain experts creating solutions directly—and the tools they reach for are multiplying by the week. That's both an opportunity and a challenge: as more people build with more AI tools, the risk of shipping ungoverned software into production grows just as fast.
   

  

 At Retool, we're building the platform that makes all of it safe to ship. Build with any AI tool you want, then deploy into one place that connects to your real business data, enforces enterprise policies automatically, and lets teams create once and reuse everywhere with shared, trusted components. The cost of building software has collapsed. The cost of governing it hasn't—and that's the problem we solve.
   

  

 Developers and domain experts have already automated over 100 million hours of work on our platform, freeing them to focus on creative problem\-solving and strategic work that drives real business value. The people closest to the problem can now build the software to solve it, safely, and within enterprise guardrails.
   

  

 Let's build the future together.
   

  

**WHY WE’RE LOOKING FOR YOU**
 We’re building AI\-native products where model behavior is part of the product, not just an implementation detail. As LLMs become more capable, the bottleneck is no longer access to models—it’s making non\-deterministic systems reliable, evaluable, and trustworthy in production.
   

  

 We’re hiring AI Engineers to own that problem end to end. This is not a role for someone who simply integrates AI APIs into features. It’s for engineers who take responsibility for how probabilistic systems behave over time, how quality is measured in the presence of variance, and how capabilities improve without regressing.
   

  

 If model regressions, subtle behavior drift, or edge\-case failures keep you up at night—and you enjoy that kind of ownership—we want to talk.
   

  

**What You’ll Do**
 As an AI Engineer, you’ll own model\-driven behavior in production systems, working across product, infrastructure, and evaluation layers. Your work will directly shape what users experience—and how confidently the team can ship. You might:
   

  

* Own the behavior of AI\-powered features across multiple product surfaces, including quality, safety, variance, and failure modes
* Design and evolve prompting, retrieval, routing, and tool\-use strategies that embrace non\-determinism while bounding its downside
* Build and maintain evaluation systems that measure model performance using statistical signals, distributions, and trends—not just pass/fail tests
* Detect, diagnose, and resolve non\-deterministic failures such as hallucinations, partial correctness, instruction drift, or sensitivity to context changes
* Define and implement guardrails, fallbacks, and degradation paths that keep systems useful even when models behave unexpectedly
* Partner with product and infra teams to decide when probabilistic behavior is “good enough” to ship—and when it isn’t
* Influence model selection, model behavior, and tool design to balance quality, cost, latency, and robustness for real user workflows


 You’ll work across the stack (e.g., TypeScript, Node.js, React), but your leverage won’t come from code volume alone—it will come from shaping runtime behavior with precision, measurement, and intent.
   

  

**This Role Is**
**WHAT THIS ROLE IS (AND IS NOT)**
* Accountable for AI behavior, not just system correctness
* Grounded in evaluation, iteration, and regression prevention under non\-determinism
* Comfortable designing systems where outputs vary, confidence is probabilistic, and correctness is contextual
* Focused on shipping dependable products on top of imperfect components


**This Role Is Not**
* Adding LLM calls to existing features and moving on
* Treating models as black boxes with undefined behavior
* Shipping AI features without owning their long\-term reliability, drift, or user trust


**The Skillset You’ll Bring**
* 6\+ years of professional engineering experience, with ownership over complex systems in production
* Demonstrated experience owning AI/LLM behavior beyond basic integration, including mitigation of variance and failure modes
* Comfort reasoning about probabilistic systems and tradeoffs (quality vs. cost, recall vs. precision, speed vs. robustness)
* Experience designing or maintaining evaluation frameworks, golden datasets, regression detection, or human\-in\-the\-loop feedback loops
* Strong product intuition—you care deeply about what “good” looks like even when outputs are non\-deterministic
* Ability to operate independently in ambiguous problem spaces and set quality standards others rely on
* Strong opinions, weakly held—you iterate quickly and adjust based on evidence and observed runtime behavior


**BONUS POINTS**
* Experience with RAG, agentic systems, or tool\-using models in production
* Familiarity with vector databases, embeddings, or retrieval pipelines
* Exposure to fine\-tuning, model routing, or post\-training techniques
* Experience building shared AI infrastructure used by multiple teams
* History of mentoring engineers on designing for non\-determinism and evaluation\-driven development


**Who You’ll Work With**
 You’ll join a small, senior team focused on advancing AI capabilities across the product. You’ll collaborate closely with product engineers, infra engineers, designers, and PMs—often acting as the final owner of AI behavior and quality before features reach users.
   

  

 Your work will set standards that others build on. If you enjoy being the person teams rely on when AI behavior matters most—and certainty is never guaranteed—you’ll thrive here.
   

  

**READY TO BUILD RELIABLE AI SYSTEMS?**
 If you’re excited to move beyond demos and take real ownership of non\-deterministic behavior in production—defining quality, preventing regressions, and turning variability into a strength—we’d love to meet you.

**Description**
 Medix Infusion is seeking a motivated and detail\-oriented Data Analyst to join our team. This entry\-level position is ideal for an individual who enjoys working with data, solving problems, and learning how analytics can support business operations and strategic decision\-making.
   

  

 The Data Analyst will assist with collecting, organizing, analyzing, and presenting data to help teams better understand performance and identify opportunities for improvement. The successful candidate will have foundational technical skills, strong attention to detail, and an eagerness to grow within a collaborative, healthcare\-focused environment.
   

  

 Medix Infusion is a technology\-driven healthcare platform dedicated to enhancing patient care and access to infusion therapies. We specialize in disease management and infusion pharmacy services for chronic and acutely ill patients, particularly those in underserved communities. We provide personalized home and in\-suite infusion therapies, including anti\-infectives, biologics, IVIG, and other injectable treatments, with the goal of making each patient’s journey as smooth as possible.
   

  

**Key Responsibilities**
* Collect, organize, and analyze data to support business operations and departmental initiatives.
* Assist with developing and maintaining SQL queries for data extraction, validation, and analysis.
* Prepare routine and ad hoc reports for business leaders and departmental stakeholders.
* Create and maintain dashboards and data visualizations using Power BI.
* Assist with cleaning, transforming, and validating data from multiple sources.

* Maintain the confidentiality and security of sensitive business, employee, and patient information.
* Perform other duties and analytical projects as assigned.
